title: WorkspaceStatus
description: data of `kriya runs status --workspace PATH --json --kup-version 1`: an envelope around the existing recovery assessment; status and semantic exit codes preserved (P-25, P-27). Belongs to the selected workspace at observation time, never to a selected trace row (P-22).

status.description: The existing recovery assessment status, verbatim.

exit_code.description: The semantic exit code the non-KUP command would have returned.

WorkspaceDescribe.description: data of `workspace.describe` (GUI M5): the read-only facts Kriya reports about a folder the desktop host picked. Nothing here classifies the folder as greenfield or brownfield; absent facts are null (the host shows Not recorded), never inferred.

workspace.description: Kriya's canonical spelling of the folder (control-plane identity input).

identity.description: sha256 workspace identity Kriya records in run manifests.

head.description: Commit Git reports for HEAD; null when unborn or not a checkout root.

dirty.description: Tracked changes or untracked files per `git status`; null when Git did not report.

changed_entries.description: Upper bound on changed paths (a rename counts its source too), capped at 1000.

reason.description: Why a fact is missing, when Git said.

ExecutionPreflight.description: data of `execution.preflight` (GUI M6): what a run in this folder would be, resolved by Kriya exactly as a terminal `kriya generate` run there would be. The host displays it and decides nothing from it; the launched process re-resolves it and refuses on any blocker.

source.description: Kriya's ConfigSource value for the user layer (packaged_default when no file was found).

directory.description: The directory configuration was discovered from (the folder itself).

fingerprint.description: Digest of the effective configuration (the resume checkpoint's own fingerprint); null when it did not load.

security.description: Security demonstration (additive; absent from an older Kriya): the file protections run against a disposable folder, each row the canonical owner's own decision.

health.description: Project health rows (additive; absent from an older Kriya): capabilities no other answer states, each with a closed state, a reason code and the configuration fields / observations that decided it.

memory.description: VERIFIED PROJECT MEMORY of the folder's repository, read now (additive; absent from an older Kriya).

approvals.description: change_review: a change is held for the person's review (human-in-the-loop). configured_mode: the resolved configuration selects another autonomy mode (shown, never changed by the app). unknown: the configuration could not be resolved.

autonomy_mode.description: The autonomy mode of the resolved configuration, verbatim.

HealthRow.description: One capability of a folder with its state (AVAILABLE, DEGRADED, UNAVAILABLE, NOT_REQUIRED, DISABLED, UNKNOWN), a closed reason code and the evidence that decided it. Derived from the resolved configuration or a read-only observation, never from a claim about a run.

SecurityDemonstration.description: One protection shown by running it: the canonical owner's own decision (BLOCKED, ALLOWED or REDACTED) about a situation built in a disposable folder, with its typed reason code and the rule that made it. No path, no content and no secret is carried.

SecurityEvidence.description: The security demonstration of a preflight: the rows, in presentation order.

stale_reason.description: EVIDENCE_CHANGED, EVIDENCE_MISSING or EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE when STALE.

why.description: "Why does Kriya know this?": the provenance, from the stored record only.

evidence_run_id.description: The control-plane run id the run's evidence store and RunRecord carry (what the cockpit knows the run by); null when it could not be determined.

ProjectMemory.description: VERIFIED PROJECT MEMORY (product/demo-72h): safe, validated facts about ONE repository, a read-only PROJECTION of verified run evidence onto the repository as it is now. A fact is CURRENT only while every evidence file still has the digest it was learned from; otherwise it is STALE with a reason code and is never reused. Carries no commands and no secrets; repository-scoped.

repository.description: The repository identity (the workspace authority's digest).

WorkspaceCreate.description: data of `workspace.create` (end-user experience): ONE new empty project folder was created by Kriya. Nothing else was written.

ConfigurationApprovalStatus.description: data of `configuration.approval_status`: which operator-controlled settings of a folder need an approval and whether a current approval covers them, exactly as `kriya authority inspect` reports it. Only the NAMES of the settings are carried; no configuration value is ever sent.

status.description: not_required: nothing in the configuration needs approval. required: a current approval does not cover it. approved: a current approval covers it. unavailable: an approval cannot be given from this application (see reason).

reason.description: no_approval | stale_approval | store_unreadable | trust_file_in_effect | trust_file_inside_workspace | store_inside_workspace | null

ConfigurationApprove.description: data of `configuration.approve`: the approval Kriya recorded (the same artifact `kriya authority approve` writes), or already_approved when a current approval already covered the reviewed configuration and nothing was written.

ProjectInitialize.description: data of `project.initialize`: Kriya created its recommended configuration file in a folder that had none. It approves nothing: the protected settings it introduces need the ordinary configuration approval.

ChangeApprovalReview.description: data of `change_approval.review`: the EXACT proposed change a review asks the person to approve, served only after Kriya re-proved it against the review's digests (per-file diff digests, candidate digest, identity). Approval-scoped: it is not the evidence store and does not depend on content_visibility. `truncated` true means the change is larger than one response can carry: the host must NOT offer approval.

status.description: The review's own status: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED or EXPIRED.

candidate_digest.description: The digest the decision must carry; the diff below is proved to be what it binds.

reason.description: The gate's reason text, verbatim (as Kriya recorded it).

policy_note.description: The part of the reason before the automated reviewer's section (why the change was held for a human).

review_summary.description: The automated reviewer's report: the text after the reviewer-section delimiter, unaltered; null when the reason has no such section.

ExecutionContext.description: data of `execution.context`: the Skills, tools and per-role model routing a run in this folder would have, from the resolved configuration and files; starts no process and touches no network. Rule text, commands, arguments, environment and credentials are never included.

ExecutionModelProbe.description: data of `execution.model_probe`: one bounded local GET /models per distinct endpoint, made now.

RuntimeCommandReview.description: data of `runtime_command.review`: the EXACT commands a runtime-command review asks the person to allow Kriya to run, served only after Kriya re-proved them against the command fingerprint the review is bound to (working directory, commands in order, input channel, stdin digest). Approval-scoped and read-only: it approves nothing; the decision is taken over the run's private review channel.

status.description: The review's own status: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED or EXPIRED.

command_fingerprint.description: The digest the decision must carry.

PendingChangeReview.description: A CHANGE review: the exact candidate (digest; files with diff digests) and Kriya's reviewer text VERBATIM (bounded).

PendingRuntimeCommandReview.description: A RUNTIME-COMMAND review (a subject distinct from a change review): the exact resolved commands Kriya asks to run to verify the application, in order, where they run, and the command fingerprint the decision must carry. Never a stdin or environment VALUE; `files` does not exist on this shape.

candidate_digest.description: Equal to command_fingerprint: the digest the decision must carry.

command_fingerprint.description: Digest over the working directory, the commands in order, the input channel and the stdin digest.

criterion.description: What the verification looks for (bounded, secret-scrubbed).

working_directory.description: The ACTUAL absolute directory the commands run in: Kriya's isolated candidate worktree.

PendingVerifierRepairAuthorization.description: A VERIFIER-DEFECT REPAIR AUTHORIZATION review (owner rulings 2026-11-13; a subject distinct from a change review and a runtime-command review): the person's SEMANTIC decision whether ONE exact verifier candidate conflicts with the canonical contract, authorizing one bounded repair of it. Everything shown is deterministic evidence Kriya recorded - the verifier's exact source and digest, the canonical contract text and digest, the gate outcome against the pre-repair owner and against the repaired owner - never a model's conclusion. `authorization_fingerprint` (= candidate_digest) covers every binding (run, plan, recovery, verifier bytes, contract, owner states, failure identities) and is what the decision must carry. `verified` is Kriya's own re-proof, at read time, that the recorded texts are the bytes the fingerprint binds; a review that is not verified is never offered for approval.

candidate_digest.description: Equal to authorization_fingerprint: the digest the decision must carry.

authorization_fingerprint.description: Digest over every binding of the authorization.

verified.description: Present in a served status: Kriya re-derived the fingerprint from the recorded bindings and re-checked every shown text against its bound digest.

question.description: The exact question the person decides.

notice.description: Kriya's fixed statement that automatic verifier repair is otherwise forbidden and what an approval does and does not do.

verifier_files.description: The verifier candidate under review: each file's path, the digest of its exact bytes and its exact source.

contract_text.description: The canonical goal/contract text, exactly as bound by contract_digest.

pre_repair_owner_files.description: The owner's implicated files BEFORE its repair (path and digest; the bytes stay in the run's memory).

repaired_owner_files.description: The same files after the owner's repair.

pre_repair_outcome.description: The deterministic gate output of this verifier against the pre-repair owner (bounded, display-redacted).

replay_outcome.description: The deterministic gate output of this verifier against the repaired owner: the failure under review (bounded, display-redacted).

PendingVerifierSemanticReview.description: A VERIFIER SEMANTIC REVIEW (VERIFIER-SEMANTIC-REVIEW-001, owner ruling 2026-11-14; a fourth subject, distinct from the replay-specific verifier-repair authorization): the person's decision whether the expectation of ONE exact INITIAL generated verifier is correct under the canonical contract. A generated verifier's pass or failure is candidate evidence, never the truth. Its decision vocabulary is its own: `expectation_valid`, `expectation_invalid`, `cannot_decide` - never approve/reject. A decided review has status DECIDED (no polarity) and the word in `decision.decision`; EXPIRED with a null decision means nobody decided, which is NOT `cannot_decide`. `semantic_fingerprint` (= candidate_digest) covers every binding (run, plan, verifier unit and bytes, goal and contract digests, the unit's plan-declared criteria and invariants, the review phase and, for a failing verifier, the failure identity). `verified` is Kriya's own read-time re-proof; a review that is not verified is never offered for a decision.

candidate_digest.description: Equal to semantic_fingerprint: the digest the decision must carry.

semantic_fingerprint.description: Digest over every binding of the review EVENT (includes the review phase and, for a failing verifier, the failure identity).

semantic_authority_fingerprint.description: What an expectation_valid decision is authority for: the exact verifier content under the exact contract (run, plan, verifier unit, verifier path and bytes, goal and contract digests, criteria and invariants). The review phase and failure identity are not in it.

verified.description: Present in a served status: Kriya re-derived the fingerprint from the recorded bindings and re-checked every shown text against its bound digest.

question.description: The exact question the person decides.

notice.description: Kriya's fixed statement of what each of the three decisions does and does not do.

decisions.description: The only decision words this review accepts.

review_phase.description: Whether the verifier passed or failed its deterministic gate; a decision for one phase is never authority for the other.

verifier_files.description: The verifier candidate under review: each file's path, the digest of its exact bytes and its exact source.

contract_text.description: The canonical goal/contract text, exactly as bound by contract_digest.

acceptance_criteria.description: The plan-declared acceptance criteria of the verifier unit (id and exact text), bound by the fingerprint.

invariants.description: The plan-declared global invariants relevant to the verifier unit (id and exact text), bound by the fingerprint.

outcome.description: The verifier's own deterministic gate output (bounded, display-redacted); shown, not bound.

RunLog.description: data of `run.log` (owner ruling 2026-11-07, the cockpit's Kriya Log): one bounded page of ONE run's real application log (`<log dir>/runs/<run id>/kriya.log`), already redacted by the logging owner and redacted again by the projection. Only what the line format guarantees is a field: `time`, `level`, `logger`, `message` (a banner or continuation line is part of the message of the record before it); no phase is inferred from text. `next_cursor` is opaque (`o<offset>`); `at_end` says the read reached the end of the file now. `available: false` with a closed `reason` is an answer, never an empty log presented as nothing having happened.

LaunchStatus.description: data of `launch.status` (GUI M6): one desktop launch read back from durable records only (launch record, RunRecord, attempt-evidence store, workspace run lock). `liveness` is DERIVED; no outcome is ever inferred from a process exit.

declined_decisions.description: Decisions the run could proceed without (skill gap/conflict, live lookup) that the desktop declined: nothing was approved, the run continued; informational only.

pending_approval.description: The review the run is waiting on (or last waited on): a CHANGE review (the exact candidate, Kriya's reviewer text) or a RUNTIME-COMMAND review (the exact commands Kriya asks to run), discriminated by `kind`. Only a PENDING review can be decided, over the run's private review channel for its own kind; the waiting process records the decision BEFORE the run continues.

approval_history.description: Earlier reviews of this launch (a retry produced a new candidate), oldest first; none of them can be decided any more.

approval_required.description: The human decision the run reached and the desktop cannot make (never auto-approved): which kind, the reason Kriya gave, and the recorded details.

liveness.description: DERIVED from the launch phase and the workspace run lock.
